correctness.rationale: With the base difference lifted to h in (−ε,ε), the increment in fiber difference satisfies |Δ|≤2a<1−2ε, so an orbit staying Bowen-close cannot jump between integer neighborhoods at successive observations. The real endpoint interval overlap is exactly (2ε−n|Δ|)_+, giving the Haar mass independent of y. The two possible cosine level roots are h=0 and h≡−2x; interior simple roots contribute 4ε²/|φ′| each, with the boundary-root cases excluded as stated. At either extremum the quadratic coefficient of |Δ| is 2aπ²; h=t/√n has bounded rescaled support and the integral of (2ε−2aπ²t²)_+ is 8ε^(3/2)/(3π√a). For the mean, m=x+h/2 is Haar and K(B)=E(2ε−B|sin(2πm)|)_+, where B=2an|sin πh|. Its small-sine density is 2/π+O(s²), giving K(B)=4ε²/(πB)+Oε(B⁻³) for B≥4ε. The region h=O(1/n) contributes O(1/n); integrating the error on its complement also contributes O(1/n). The two signs of h and ∫dh/sin(πh)=(log n)/π+O(1) with this cutoff give exactly 4ε²/(aπ²). Strict and nonstrict boundaries differ by area zero. These bounds are for fixed a, ε, not uniform for shrinking radii.
